jobs.description:
AI is moving fast, and at VELUX we are building the capability to move with it. This is your opportunity to shape how AI becomes part of everyday work across a global organisation, helping colleagues turn new tools and possibilities into new habits, stronger capabilities and measurable business value.

Meet your future team

You will join our newly established Enablers team, reporting to the VP of Enablers and working closely with colleagues across the AI Centre of Excellence, P&O and business functions throughout the VELUX Group.

The team's mission is to accelerate the successful adoption of AI across the organisation by enabling people, driving behavioural change and ensuring new technologies create measurable business value. Working in a highly collaborative environment, you will engage with stakeholders across functions, markets and organisational levels to help AI become a natural part of how we work.

As our AI Change Lead, you will play a pivotal role in transforming AI from a promising capability into a practical and valuable part of employees' daily work.

What We Offer

In this newly created role, you will lead the people side of our AI transformation. While training, enablement and community-building are important tools, your primary focus will be driving real behavioural change and business impact through effective AI adoption across VELUX.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Own and continuously evolve AI upskilling programme, including learning journeys, training curricula and workshops tailored to different audiences and maturity levels.

• Drive the adoption of AI tools through onboarding, guidance and best-practice sharing, ensuring new solutions are embraced and used effectively.

• Build and maintain an AI adoption ecosystem through playbooks, documentation, team briefings and self-service resources that empower colleagues to succeed independently.

• Establish and grow an AI Champions network and facilitate community activities, office hours and knowledge-sharing forums to create engagement and momentum.

• Support the rollout of new AI solutions and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure effective implementation across the organisation.

• Measure adoption, usage and business impact, using data and insights to continuously optimise initiatives and prioritise future efforts.

What You Will Bring

As a person, you are pragmatic, curious, outcome-oriented and energised by helping others learn, grow and succeed. You are passionate about helping people embrace new technology and have a proven ability to drive change in large organisations. You combine strong communication and facilitation skills with a practical understanding of technology and the opportunities it creates for employees and businesses.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Have solid experience within learning and enablement, change management, digital adoption or a related field in a large international organisation.

• Have successfully designed and delivered enterprise-wide capability-building programmes that resulted in measurable behavioural change.

• Are an engaging facilitator and communicator who can make complex topics easy to understand and relevant for diverse audiences.

• Can build credibility with both business stakeholders and technical colleagues.

• Are fluent in English, both written and spoken.

Ready to apply?

Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis until we have the right match.

All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

About VELUX

In the VELUX Group, we offer you a world of opportunities and the chance to create a bright future. From the forefront of the roof window category, we enable those who live, work and play under the roof transform their spaces and live a healthier everyday life with more daylight and fresh air.

The VELUX Group is an international, family-owned business with strong financial roots and each year we can create real impact by reinvesting in society, our employees and planet through our foundations. With 20 production companies in 12 countries and sales companies in 37 countries, our products are widely available. We employ around 12,000 people, and our company is headquartered in Denmark. Alongside the rest of our values, “courage” and “mutual respect” define our actions every day and how we wish to contribute to the world.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At VELUX Residential, we believe in fostering a diverse workplace for everyone to thrive, develop and perform at their best, and where you feel welcome, respected and valued. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all, whether you are applying for a role or already a part of VELUX Residential. That means we recruit, hire, train and promote people based on their skills and potential without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, age, neurodiversity, disability, protected veteran status, national origin, sexual orientation or any other basis prohibited by applicable law.

We value diversity and strive to ensure that our employment decisions are fair and inclusive, focusing only on what truly matters: your qualifications and how you can contribute to our shared mission and success.

Your impact begins here

As Global Search and Evaluation Director, you will help decide which external science becomes part of Novo’s future portfolio. You will find promising drug assets and enabling technologies, then lead their evaluation from first look through due diligence. Your recommendations will shape business development priorities across diabetes, obesity, liver and cardiovascular disease, blood and endocrine disorders and Consumer Rx – helping bring the right ideas from lab and clinic closer to the people who need them.

What you’ll bring

You combine scientific depth with commercial judgement, and you are known in the biotech and investor communities. You will bring:

• A Master’s degree in business or life science.

• 12+ years of relevant experience with a Master’s degree, or 10+ years with an MD or PhD – for example from consultancy, an M&A house, an in-house corporate development role or an equivalent R&D role.

• An extensive professional network in the biotech and venture capital communities, particularly related to metabolic diseases.

• A proven track record in project management, including leading complex, cross-functional work to clear decisions.

• The ability to analyse complex ideas and data and turn them into clear, well-founded recommendations for senior stakeholders.

• Strong written communication and presentation skills, and an outgoing approach to networking, collaboration and stakeholder management.

• Strong strategic business and financial acumen, paired with real curiosity about life sciences and medicine.

• A self-driven, goal-oriented way of working, with the ability to handle ambiguity and change in a dynamic environment.

Useful, but not essential:

• An MD or PhD degree.

• Research and medical training, ideally in a relevant medical field.

• Business development and licensing experience covering pharmaceutical drug discovery and development.

What you’ll do

Search, Evaluation & Intelligence is the primary entry point for external drug and technology opportunities at Novo. In this role, you will lead the evaluation of business development opportunities and help Novo move quickly on the ones that matter most.

• Identify novel pipeline assets and cutting-edge enabling technologies across several modalities in Novo’s therapy areas of interest.

• Lead in-depth, cross-functional evaluations and due diligence, from initial assessment to clear recommendations.

• Support Business Development colleagues during negotiation of licences and collaborations, in alignment with Search, Evaluation & Intelligence.

• Build and maintain business development opportunity landscapes, and continuously feed insights into business development priorities and therapy area strategies.

• Help establish Novo as the preferred partner in relevant therapy areas by engaging actively with biotech companies, venture capital firms and large-cap pharma.

• Represent Novo at partnering events, scientific conferences and other relevant networking events.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the global evaluation team in Search, Evaluation & Intelligence, part of Global Business Development, with colleagues based mainly in Denmark and Cambridge, MA, US. You will report to the Head of Global Evaluation. This is an individual contributor role without direct reports.

You will work closely with Novo’s Business Development teams in Denmark and Cambridge, and with stakeholders across the value chain – from R&D to Commercial and beyond – to build alignment and keep evaluations moving at pace.

Externally, you will draw on and grow your network across biotech, venture capital and large-cap pharma, working with start-ups, established companies and investors to turn promising science into partnerships that create value for both sides.

What you can expect here

You will work where science, strategy and partnering meet, with a direct view of innovation across one of the world’s largest life sciences ecosystems. Your expertise will be trusted, your voice will count in portfolio and partnering discussions, and you will be expected to make clear calls, own them and follow through.

You will build new skills through cross value chain collaboration and grow alongside colleagues on the job and through relevant learning offerings. Clear performance expectations and a culture that rewards results will support you in doing your best work.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 940,800.00 y 1,448,700.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to find the science that shapes Novo’s future portfolio – and help bring it to the people who need it – apply for the Global Search and Evaluation Director role before 22 October. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To submit your application, please upload your CV and motivational letter online (click on Apply and follow the instructions). Internal candidates are kindly requested to inform their line managers before applying.

Are you an experienced validation professional who enjoys solving complex challenges at the intersection of product quality, compliance and logistics? Join us as our new Senior Validation Professional in a role with strong international scope, where you will collaborate across technical, quality, logistics and regulatory functions to shape robust solutions and take on increasing responsibility.

This role offers the opportunity to apply your expertise across transport validation and transport control, gain broad exposure to global stakeholders, and influence an area of growing strategic importance and responsibility. If you are ready to make an impact in global transport validation, we encourage you to apply.

What you’ll do

As Senior Validation Professional, you will combine hands-on validation work with close cross-functional collaboration to solve complex transport challenges, improve established processes and help ensure the reliable distribution of our products.

You will independently plan and execute complex transport qualification and validation activities for transport lanes, equipment and products, translating applicable Good Distribution Practice (GDP) requirements and business needs into practical, documented solutions within established procedures and governance.  As a senior subject-matter expert, you will support cross-functional stakeholders, contribute to improvements and act as a sparring partner for validation colleagues.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Execute transport qualification and validation. Define and carry out activities for lanes, equipment and products, and author and review protocols, risk assessments, risk reports and validation plans.

• 
Strengthen transport compliance and control. Support compliant end-to-end distribution processes, contribute to the assessment and mitigation of transport risks, and review new or updated Product Specific Requirements.

• 
Support submissions, audits and inspections. Provide transport validation input to Regulatory Affairs and prepare, explain and present validation documentation when required.

• 
Contribute to projects and improvements. Bring transport validation expertise to cross-functional supply chain initiatives and execute agreed improvements and validation strategy initiatives.

• 
Maintain the validated state. Author and review SOPs, perform and review activities to maintain the validated state, and provide technical input to deviations and change requests.

What you’ll bring

We imagine that you have a relevant degree in pharmaceutical sciences, engineering, life sciences or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.  You also bring:

• 
Solid experience with qualification or validation in a regulated pharmaceutical environment, ideally including transport validation, distribution or cold-chain logistics.

• 
A strong understanding of GDP and the ability to apply relevant health authority requirements to transport activities.

• 
Experience preparing and reviewing validation documentation and risk assessments.

• 
The confidence to independently handle complex activities, make well-supported technical judgements and communicate recommendations clearly.

• 
Strong collaboration skills and the ability to turn technical requirements into practical guidance for colleagues.

• 
Strong written and spoken English.

• 
Experience supporting regulatory submissions and presenting in audits or inspections would be an advantage.

We are looking for an experienced professional who thrives in a complex, global environment and knows how to create alignment across diverse stakeholder groups. You communicate clearly and confidently influence decisions, create alignment and drive practical solutions when priorities and requirements differ.

You take a structured, risk-based approach, keeping product quality and patient safety at the centre of your decisions. You balance compliance with operational needs, follow activities through to completion and recognise when escalation is needed. You also enjoy sharing your knowledge, constructively challenging assumptions and helping colleagues move forward.

Who you’ll work with

Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS) is responsible for manufacturing and supplying Novo’s products to patients worldwide. We combine operational excellence, innovation, and a strong quality mindset to ensure reliable delivery of medicines while continuously improving our processes and expanding our global manufacturing network.

You will join Global Compliance and Transport Control (GC&TC), part of Global Logistics and Distribution. We help ensure a compliant and resilient global supply chain and keep the organisation ready for inspections. Through transport validation and compliance activities, we support product submissions and the addition of new production facilities and warehouses to our logistics network, enabling business growth.

What you can expect here

At Novo, you can expect a role where your scientific judgement matters, your ideas are listened to, and your work helps move complex development projects forward. You will have opportunities to deepen your expertise, build cross-functional influence and grow in a collaborative environment where initiative is encouraged. You will be supported to perform at your best and trusted to take ownership, while contributing to work that helps create progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Job title: Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Reporting to: Chief Executive Officer

Department: Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Location: Bagsværd, Denmark. Some travel is expected.

The position

Novo Nordisk is seeking a Senior Vice President to lead Corporate Strategy & Business Development, a newly established organisation that brings together two critical capabilities shaping the company's long-term strategic direction and growth.

Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of Executive Management, you will hold an enterprise-wide mandate to shape corporate strategy, inform strategic choices, and identify and execute external opportunities that strengthen Novo Nordisk's future position.

The role requires a senior executive who combines strategic perspective, deep business understanding and sound judgement with the ability to translate strategic priorities into decisions, partnerships and transactions that deliver long-term value.

Key responsibilities

As Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development, you will lead a global organisation of approximately 60 employees across Corporate Strategy and Business Development. You will work closely with the CEO, Executive Management and senior leaders across Novo Nordisk.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead the development and regular review of Novo Nordisk's corporate strategy in close collaboration with the CEO and Executive Management.

• Shape strategic choices on where to compete, how to win and which capabilities to build to support the company's long-term ambitions.

• Lead the full business development value chain, including opportunity identification, due diligence, valuation, transaction execution, contracting, post-deal integration and alliance management.

• Connect internal capabilities and portfolio priorities with external opportunities, including strategic partnerships, collaborations and acquisitions.

• Ensure rigorous strategic and financial assessment, effective governance and clear accountability for value creation across business development activities.

• Build trusted relationships with key internal and external stakeholders and represent Novo Nordisk in strategic partnerships and transactions.

• Lead and develop a high-performing global organisation across Corporate Strategy and Business Development, fostering collaboration and strong leadership.

Your experience and leadership profile

We are seeking an accomplished senior executive with a demonstrated ability to shape enterprise strategy, lead complex business development activities and influence decision-making at the highest organisational levels.

The successful candidate will bring:

• Substantial senior leadership experience in corporate strategy, business development or related disciplines, gained within the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry, investment banking, management consulting or a comparable global environment.

• A strong track record of shaping enterprise strategy and leading complex strategic partnerships, transactions or acquisitions.

• Broad scientific and commercial understanding, combined with strong financial acumen and the ability to assess strategic opportunities and risks.

• The credibility and judgement to advise and constructively challenge the CEO and Executive Management, and to build alignment among senior leaders across a complex global organisation.

• Demonstrated people leadership, with the ability to develop strong leadership teams and build diverse, inclusive and high-performing organisations.

• Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills, together with the integrity and external credibility required to represent Novo Nordisk in significant partnerships and transactions.

You are a collaborative and decisive leader who combines long-term strategic thinking with the ability to deliver results. You exercise sound judgement in complex situations, challenge established thinking when necessary and build trust across different perspectives and interests.

Application and further information

Please submit your application, including a CV and a cover letter outlining your motivation, no later than 30 October 2026.

For further information, please contact Executive Search Advisor Kristoffer Baadsgaard at +45 30 77 56 05.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

The Department of Chemistry invites applicants for a 2-year postdoc position within Theoretical Catalysis under the ERC-SyG DEMI, starting from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  DEMI (Directed Evolution of Metastable Electrocatalyst Interfaces for Energy Conversion) is an ERC Synergy Grant funded by the European Research Council Executive Agency.

  In the Theoretical Catalysis group, we aim to provide a deeper understanding of catalytic processes and catalytic materials by atomic scale simulations. We have a special interest in electrocatalytic reactions and high entropy materials, and the methods include DFT-simulations, machine learning potentials, Monte Carlo simulations and statistical analysis. We enjoy a close collaboration with experimental groups, both at the department and other universities in Denmark and abroad. The DEMI project is a collaboration with research groups from University of Bern, Ruhr University Bochum and Helmholtz-Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg.

  The Theoretical Catalysis group is part of Center for High Entropy Alloy Catalysis.

  The successful candidate holds a Ph.D. in computational chemistry, DFT-simulations, physical modelling or a similar background. Experience with theoretical catalysis or electrocatalysis is a benefit.

  The postdoc’s duty is primarily research within Theoretical Catalysis but may include performance of other duties.

  Further information on the Department is linked at www.chem.ku.dk. Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Jan Rossmeisl, phone +4550719584 or email: jan.rossmeisl@chem.ku.dk.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Are you studying computer science, software engineering, AI, or a related subject- and looking for more than an ordinary student job? Do you enjoy understanding complicated problems, building software that real people use, and exploring how AI and agents are changing the way software is developed?

We are looking for a Student Software Engineer to join the engineering team behind Omnidocs Create, its integrations, and related engineering projects.

You will work as part of our engineering team on real product challenges across frontend and backend development. You will also help us develop how we use AI and agentic engineering workflows to understand systems, investigate problems, plan solutions, implement changes, and verify results.

You do not need professional experience with our technology stack. We care more about how you think, how quickly you learn, and how you approach problems when the answer is not immediately obvious.

The basics

• 12–15 hours per week during the semester.

• Flexible scheduling around classes and exams.

• Possibility of additional hours during quieter study periods and holidays.

• Competitive salary.

• Opportunities to grow into greater technical ownership and responsibility.

What you will work on

• Contribute to established production codebases and new engineering projects.

• Build and improve functionality across our products and integrations, primarily using .NET, C#, and Blazor.

• Connect frontend experiences to backend APIs and services.

• Work on integrations and related engineering projects, sometimes involving unfamiliar systems or technologies.

• Help turn complex business rules and document workflows into understandable product experiences.

• Investigate defects, improve tests, and strengthen code quality.

• Work with product, design, and engineering colleagues to understand problems and shape solutions.

• Participate in code reviews, planning, technical discussions, and product demonstrations.

• Use AI tools and agents to explore code, plan, prototype, implement, test, and document.

• Critically evaluate and verify AI-generated work rather than accepting it at face value.

As you grow, you may take ownership of features and engineering projects from problem definition through delivery.

Who we are looking for

• Are pursuing a relevant degree at ITU, DTU, DIKU, or another comparable institution.

• Have a foundation in programming from your studies, personal projects, employment, or open-source work.

• Enjoy breaking complicated or ambiguous problems into understandable steps.

• Take initiative when you encounter something unfamiliar.

• Can explain your thinking, including uncertainty, mistakes, and trade-offs.

• Are interested in AI-assisted and agentic ways of working.

• Want to learn through feedback, collaboration, and practical responsibility.

• Can communicate effectively in English.

• Are able to work regularly from our Copenhagen office.

You do not need previous professional experience with Blazor or .NET. Experience with another programming language or web framework can provide an equally good foundation.

Helpful, but not required

Experience or experimentation with any of the following is a plus:

• C#, .NET, Blazor, React, TypeScript, Java, Python, or similar technologies.

• Web applications, APIs, databases, automated testing, or Git.

• UX, accessibility, responsive design, or component libraries.

• Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or other AI development tools.

• AI agents, MCP, automation, or AI-assisted prototyping.

• University, personal, hackathon, or open-source software projects.

We do not expect you to arrive as an expert. We expect you to be interested enough to investigate, experiment, and learn.

The company

For over 20 years, Omnidocs has been redefining productivity in document generation. Born as a consultancy and developed into a SaaS business, we help organizations create better documents and presentations through software, automation, and design.

Today, the Omnidocs Group has almost 200 professionals across several international offices. You will join a collaborative environment where you can work closely with experienced engineers, product colleagues, and designers while developing your own technical skills and responsibilities.

What we offer

• Meaningful responsibility in live production software.

• A dedicated engineering mentor and regular feedback.

• Close collaboration with experienced engineers, product colleagues, and designers.

• Flexibility around classes, exams, and university projects.

• Opportunities to explore and develop modern AI and agentic engineering workflows.

• The possibility of connecting university projects or a thesis to relevant engineering challenges.

• Career development opportunities and the possibility of continuing with Omnidocs after graduation when there is a mutual fit and an available position.

• An informal workplace in the heart of Christianshavn.

• Lunch scheme, social activities, sports activities, and other employee benefits.

How to apply

Please apply through our recruitment system and upload your CV. Links to GitHub, a portfolio, or projects are welcome but optional.

As part of the application, we will ask you a few short questions about your education, something you have built, how you approach unfamiliar problems, your experience with AI-assisted development, and a situation where you took ownership.

You are welcome to use AI tools when preparing your application. We are more interested in authentic examples and personal reflection than perfectly polished answers.

Please use the dedicated application link rather than sending your application by email.

Omnidocs encourages applicants of all backgrounds to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team.

Processing of personal data

By registering in our HR system, BambooHR, and uploading your application and CV, you accept that Omnidocs stores the registered data and information included in the uploaded documents. All information is used solely for recruitment purposes and will be deleted within 12 months of upload.

Please do not include sensitive personal data in your application or CV, such as CPR number or information about race, religion, trade union membership, or health.

You can read more about Omnidocs' guidelines for processing personal data here:

https://omnidocs.com/processing-of-personal-data-in-the-context-of-recruitment/

jobs.occupation: Consultancy in Otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery combined with a clinical professorship in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology
jobs.description:
A clinical position as consultant of Otorhinolaryngology at the Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical professor in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the professorship and the consultancy.

The advertisement for the professorship is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About the department

The Department of Otorhinolaryngology and Audiology is responsible for the full spectrum of diagnostics and treatment within the ENT and audiological fields, encompassing both general patient care and highly specialized services. A total of more than 100 clinically active physicians is employed within the department. In addition, there is a high level of research activity, including among the clinical staff. The department currently has five formally affiliated professors, three of whom are clinical professors in otorhinolaryngology. As a university hospital department, it also has teaching obligations at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including for healthcare professionals beyond the medical field of both the primary and secondary health sector.

Clinical functions and focus areas of the department

The consultant position in head and neck surgery requires a strong interest and proven surgical expertise within malignant head and neck surgery. The ideal candidate will demonstrate solid experience in teaching and research, including involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate education, as well as supervision of PhD students. Emphasis is placed on candidates with a robust, long-standing, and continuous research background. The candidate is expected to have extensive knowledge and research experience with head and neck cancer epidemiology and documented experience with national registries and particularly with HPV-driven head and neck cancer. A broad knowledge of benign ENT conditions is also expected. Further the candidate should be active and involved in thyroid cancer research.

The position offers significant opportunities for further specialization and skill development within advanced surgical techniques, including the potential for training in robotic surgery. The consultant will also be expected to take on administrative responsibilities such as patient triage and task coordination.

As the department provides highly specialized ENT services at a university level, applicants must have documented surgical experience and a demonstrated research interest.

Applicants must submit documentation of board certification in Otorhinolaryngology. According to the regulations of the Capital Region of Denmark, applicants must have held a specialist certification for at least five years to be appointed as a consultant at Rigshospitalet, unless an exemption is granted. Furthermore, applicants must provide evidence of clinical experience within head and neck surgery, as well as documentation of scientific and educational activities.

Strong collaboration skills are essential, including the ability to work professionally and constructively in interdisciplinary teams.

Organizationally, the consultant will report to the Head of Department. For professional matters related specifically to head and neck surgery, reference will be made to the lead consultant in that subspecialty.

We offer a dynamic and rewarding position in a busy and active department housed in brand-new, state-of-the-art facilities. The position includes excellent opportunities for involvement in research and clinical development.

Work Schedule: The position includes on-call duty (approximately every 14 days), shared equally among the department’s consultants.

Salary and terms of employment will follow the applicable collective agreement.

Please note: The position is subject to regulations requiring a child protection certificate ("børneattest"). Employment is contingent upon the ability to present a clean certificate.

Research and teaching

With the establishment of the new position as Consultant in Otorhinolaryngology and Clinical Professor in Oto-rhino-laryngology with special focus on Head & Neck Surgery, the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology seek to significantly strengthen leadership and strategic development within clinical research and teaching. The professorship is conceived as a pivotal academic and clinical role that will unify and advance research activities across the specialty, with a particular emphasis on translational and interdisciplinary head and neck research.

The position will serve as an academic anchor not only for Rigshospitalet but also for Nordsjællands Hospital and, more broadly, for Region Østdanmark (RØST), with the explicit ambition of fostering coordinated research efforts across Eastern Denmark. The clinical professor is expected to provide academic leadership, facilitate collaboration between hospital departments and regional research environments, and contribute to the development of shared research strategies and priorities across institutions.

In research, the position entails responsibility for initiating, leading, and consolidating high-quality clinical and translational research programmes within head and neck surgery and related disciplines. This includes strengthening existing research groups, promoting multicentre and cross-regional studies, supporting early-career researchers, and ensuring integration of research activities across hospitals within RØST. The professor will play a key role in attracting external funding, enhancing national and international visibility, and embedding research as a core component of clinical practice throughout Eastern Denmark.

In teaching, the position carries responsibility for academic leadership in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education within otorhinolaryngology and head and neck surgery. The professor will contribute to curriculum development, pedagogical innovation, and supervision at all levels, ensuring alignment between clinical training, academic standards, and regional workforce needs. Teaching activities will be coordinated across clinical sites, thereby supporting a unified and high-quality educational environment for medical students, residents, and fellows within RØST.

Overall, the position is designed to function as a unifying professorship that integrates research, teaching, and clinical excellence across Nordsjællands Hospital, the wider hospital network in RØST, and academic partners, thereby strengthening the academic foundation and future development of the specialty across Eastern Denmark.

Qualifications

Applicants must be board-certified specialist in Oto-rhino-laryngology.

Conditions

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the professorship) and to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the professorship. Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as consultants at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

Salary and Employment Conditions

Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management. As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will hold a 1st Line of Defence role with clear ownership of the technical methodologies used to evaluate AI models and AI-enabled solutions, and of the technical requirements for the platforms that support their evaluation and ongoing monitoring. You will translate business-owned risk and control needs into clear methods, metrics, data, evidence, traceability and platform capabilities that can be implemented consistently across the Bank's technology landscape.

This is a unique opportunity to shape a consistent, scalable and evidence-based capability through which the business identifies, evaluates, monitors and manages AI model risk.

This role can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

**What You Will Be Doing

**The AI Model Assessment team is a business-owned control capability that performs evidence-based assessments of AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. We work with business owners, developers, engineers and platform teams to understand how solutions operate, define the evidence required for assessment, and establish the evaluation and monitoring capabilities needed to identify, assess and manage model risk where it arises.

Our mission is to enable responsible innovation by providing the business with a consistent and scalable framework for evaluating AI systems, monitoring their performance and risk, and demonstrating that appropriate controls are operating effectively.

As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will own the evaluation methodology and define the technical requirements for the platforms, tooling and data capabilities used by the 1st Line of Defence to evaluate and monitor AI models and AI-enabled solutions. Your mandate is to ensure that the business has robust, implementable and auditable means to assess its AI risks and controls. Your focus will be on specifying what the evaluation and monitoring capability must deliver rather than owning software development or platform operations.

You will work closely with the independent 2nd Line AI model risk function, which sets the overarching risk framework and provides oversight and constructive challenge. You will translate that framework into practical evaluation methodologies, technical requirements and business-owned controls, provide transparent evidence of how requirements are implemented, and support the resolution of identified gaps.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• Owning, developing and maintaining the methodology for evaluating AI models and AI-enabled solutions, including evaluation objectives, test approaches, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Defining the functional and technical requirements for evaluation and monitoring platforms that enable risk management, including data ingestion, test execution, metric calculation, observability, evidence capture, reporting, access controls and auditability.

• Translating model risk, business and assessment requirements into reusable evaluation methods, representative datasets, metrics, thresholds, monitoring indicators and structured evidence requirements.

• Determining how AI system architectures, components, dependencies and data flows affect evaluation scope, test design, monitoring coverage and the technical capabilities required from supporting platforms.

• Defining platform-agnostic requirements that support evaluation and monitoring across environments such as AWS Bedrock and AgentCore, Databricks, Azure OpenAI and embedded third-party AI platforms.

• Setting requirements for reproducibility and end-to-end traceability across models, prompts, datasets, configurations, system components, evaluation results, monitoring signals and changes over time.

• Prioritising opportunities to standardise and automate evaluation and monitoring activities, and working with evaluators, platform owners and engineers to convert approved control requirements into practical platform capabilities.

• Engaging with the Second Line model risk function to interpret applicable requirements, demonstrate how they are operationalised, respond to constructive challenge, and ensure that evaluation and monitoring evidence supports effective independent oversight.

• Proven experience designing or governing AI/ML evaluation methodologies, including test objectives, datasets, metrics, thresholds, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Experience translating evaluation, monitoring, risk and control needs into functional and technical requirements for platforms, tooling, data pipelines and reporting capabilities.

• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, business-owned model risk management and controls, technical assurance, MLOps, LLMOps, AI platforms or AI observability.

• Familiarity with cloud AI services or enterprise AI platforms; experience with AWS Bedrock or AgentCore, Databricks or Mosaic AI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable platforms is an advantage.

• Strong understanding of evaluation and monitoring principles, including representative datasets, experiment configuration, metric design, regression testing, monitoring indicators, traceability and evidence capture.

• Ability to distinguish methodology and requirements ownership from platform implementation, while collaborating effectively with engineers and platform owners. Python or similar tools for analysis, prototyping or investigation are an advantage, but software development is not the primary focus of the role.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to articulate evaluation, monitoring, risk and control requirements across business, assessment, platform, engineering, architecture, data and risk functions.

Experience with AI evaluation or observability technologies, for example Phoenix or comparable tools, is an advantage but is not a prerequisite.

**What We Offer You

The team combines technical AI evaluation expertise with model risk management and works across the Bank's AI initiatives. In this role, you will connect evaluators with platform, engineering, architecture and data teams by defining the methods and technical requirements their solutions must support, ensuring that risk ownership and control evidence remain anchored in the business.

If you are an experienced accounting professional who enjoys taking ownership, working independently, and being part of a collaborative team, this could be exactly the opportunity you have been looking for.

At Gubra, we are experiencing continued growth and development. As our business expands, so do the opportunities for our employees to develop professionally and take on increasing responsibility. In this role, you will become part of our finance function where teamwork, trust, and continuous improvement are highly valued.

A broad accounting role with responsibility across multiple areas

As Financial Accountant, you will be responsible for a variety of accounting and controlling activities spanning day-to-day bookkeeping, reconciliations, month-end closing activities, reporting support, and audit preparation.

You will have ownership of your own areas while working closely with your colleagues in Finance. We take pride in supporting one another and working together to ensure successful month-end closings, reporting deadlines, audits, and daily operations.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Managing accounts receivable, including invoicing, cash registrations, reminders, and communication with customers' finance departments

• Maintaining and managing the fixed asset register, including verification of physical assets and correct accounting treatment

• Handling lease accounting in accordance with IFRS 16

• Performing foreign currency revaluations on currency accounts

• Acting as system owner for Corpay, PLEO, and e-conomic

• Preparing statutory and regulatory reporting, including submissions to Statistics Denmark and other authorities

• Supporting colleagues with accounting- and finance-related questions

• Participating in month-end closing activities, reconciliations, and audit preparation

• Supporting ad hoc tasks across the group's legal entities

As you grow in the role, you will have the opportunity to expand your responsibilities and actively influence how we develop our finance processes and controls.

An experienced accounting professional with a proactive mindset

• You likely have 5+ years of experience from a finance function where you have worked independently with bookkeeping, reconciliations, month-end closing, and financial controls.

• A structured and detail-oriented approach to your work

• The ability to work independently and take responsibility for your areas

• A positive and collaborative mindset with a willingness to support colleagues across the organization

• Professional communication skills in both Danish and English, written and spoken

Experience from an international company with entities in multiple countries is considered an advantage, but not a requirement. Likewise, experience with Corpay, PLEO, and/or e-conomic is beneficial but not essential.

We are particularly interested in someone who is curious and analytical. You notice when something does not look right, investigate the underlying cause, and work proactively to find a solution rather than simply reporting the deviation.

Your new team

You will join a Finance team consisting of four colleagues, including yourself. We work closely together, share knowledge, and support one another in delivering high-quality financial operations.

The role can be structured as either a full-time or part-time position (32-37 hours per week), depending on your preferences and qualifications.

We look forward to welcoming a colleague who enjoys being part of a team while maintaining ownership of their own responsibilities.

What we offer

• A broad and independent role in a collaborative Finance team

• A full-time or part-time position (32-37 hours per week)

• Real responsibility and ownership from day one

• The opportunity to influence processes, workflows, and internal controls

• Flexible working arrangements, including the possibility of working from home

• Ongoing opportunities to develop your role and responsibilities

• An informal and positive working environment

• Dedicated colleagues and a strong team spirit

• Competitive salary based on qualifications

• Pension scheme and health insurance

• Start date as soon as possible, although we are happy to wait for the right candidate

About Gubra

Gubra is a disease-agnostic techbio company specialized in peptide-based drug discovery and development as well as preclinical contract research services striving for excellence at all levels. We insist on doing things efficiently - and often differently - to reach the results we aim for. Our vision is to become leaders in the path towards a more sustainable and healthier world. We do that by facilitating the discovery of new medicine, and by acting and inspiring others to fight the ongoing climate and biodiversity crises.

Gubra’s activities are focused on the early stages of drug development and are organised in two main highly synergistic business areas: Biotech and CRO Services. We generate our revenue by performing research for life science companies as well as by partnering projects from our discovery and development pipeline.

Our therapeutic focus is within metabolic and fibrotic diseases, and we specialize in in vivo pharmacology, ex vivo assays, drug profiling, histology, stereology and whole brain and organ imaging. People are our greatest asset, and our team consists of around 320 employees of which many are located in Hørsholm, Denmark. The mix of people from different cultures and educational backgrounds combined with our entrepreneurial mindset have greatly impacted our working environment, which is characterized by entrepreneurial drive, scientific curiosity, and teamwork – we join forces!

jobs.occupation: (Senior) Product Creation Learning Partner – Maternity Cover (Minimum 12 Months)
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building change management and learning capabilities and fostering a learning culture at scale? Do you thrive when working with tools and processes, and are you naturally curious about finding new ways to use them? If so, you could be our Senior Product Creation Learning Partner during a maternity cover of at least 12 months.

At 3Shape, Product Creation is our term for R&D. It represents the organization responsible for developing and improving our products across hardware, software, engineering, and related product-development disciplines.

We are looking for an experienced learning partner to join us on a fixed-term maternity cover. In this role, you will build and embed a scalable capability framework that ensures Product Creation teams are equipped to work effectively across processes, tools, and ways of working.

During the maternity-cover period, you will use your stakeholder-engagement skills and your ability to align and influence across organizational levels and functions. You will combine these strengths with solid experience in building and maintaining training frameworks and structures that fit the organization’s needs.

You will be part of the Product Creation Excellence (PCE) team, which consists of around 10 people, all based in Denmark. Together, we enable Product Creation and adjacent functions across processes, training, tools, strategy, and transformation.

Core Responsibilities

Training framework & architecture

• Define the learning and capability framework and structures that support tool and process adoption, ways of working, and competence building: Standardize how training is designed, deployed, and maintained (including anchoring structures, super-user and ambassador methodologies, communities of practice, learning journeys, etc.).

• Continuously improve and expand the learning and capability framework and plan for Product Creation in collaboration with the Product Creation team.

• Develop and anchor training: Enable and support the organization to own and deliver training locally where appropriate, while ensuring central support and training structures are available where needed.

Capability mapping and training roll-out

• Continuously map and prioritize training needs with stakeholders based on business needs, maturity across technical functions, necessity, and criticality.

• Define and drive rollout plans in collaboration with functional owners and/or the PCE team.

• Establish regular cadences for training areas and structures, ensuring an appropriate frequency of training events, reviews of training materials, trainer setup and coaching, and cycles for communities of practice and other learning environments.

Integration with business & transformation

• Ensure alignment with transformation initiatives and operating model changes.

• Support change management and the adoption of new practices.

Capability tracking & improvement

• Define and follow up on KPIs for capability building (e.g., adoption, proficiency, and coverage).

• Drive feedback loops and the continuous improvement of the training setup.

• Maintain an overview of capability gaps and critical skill needs.

This role may involve some travel.

Ideal profile:

For this role, we believe a good fit is someone who can bring:

• Experience in building learning frameworks in complex medical regulated R&D or technology organizations (including experience with different training and learning models, e.g., train-the-trainer, communities of practice, coaching, and online training).

• A collaborative, team-oriented mindset. We depend on strong teamwork within the PCE team and across other teams and functions, so it is essential that you thrive when working with others to solve challenges and realize opportunities.

• An understanding of and/or interest in how different profiles learn, with the ability to balance technical tool training with soft skills such as leadership.

• Experience with change management and the large-scale rollout and/or adoption of new processes, preferably in a large R&D or other technical environment.

• Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to build bridges between technical and non-technical functions.

• The ability to drive adoption without formal authority.

Join us in shaping a company culture that makes Monday mornings worth it.

At 3Shape, you will join an international R&D environment in central Copenhagen, working closely with advanced hardware, software, and engineering teams that develop products to improve dental care globally. You will have the opportunity to shape learning and capability-building practices and see your work make a direct difference for colleagues.

We are a vibrant, visionary, and international place to work. But most of all, we are a diverse group of over 50 different nationalities who all contribute to a thriving company culture. We partake in social clubs, monthly social activities, and various in-team activities as well. If that’s not enough, then add on:

• Central Copenhagen location.

• A globally recognized technology company.

• An attractive healthcare package to keep you fit and well.

• Breakfast every day and a delicious, healthy lunch prepared by our private chefs.

• A joint purpose: to enable dentists to provide superior dental care to every patient, every time.

Apply Now

Join us for a maternity cover of at least 12 months and be part of a team improving treatment and care in a meaningful industry. We encourage all qualified professionals who are passionate about building strong learning capabilities in a complex product-development environment to apply.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis; however, we plan to conduct interviews in October and November.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.
